title: The roadmap gets re-weighed as a whole, and notes stay short
why: Your question, Oct 26: are we rewriting notes instead of appending, and re-weighing the order instead of putting each new item at the front? Audit, Oct 26 at roadmap 9517045: mostly not.
note: Measured Oct 26 at roadmap 9517045 (101 commits since Oct 22). Notes: 85 of 135 note edits were appends, 43 rewrites, 7 cuts; 15 of 84 notes pass 300 words, done steps included (c22 1,157 words). Order: in 101 commits no existing step moved, except one overwrite and its restore; all 14 steps filed since Oct 25 landed in the top 12 of about 40 open steps, the last four at ranks 0 to 3, by squeezing (107.9, 107.95 ... 107.98). 21 design, rollout and later steps have not been touched since Oct 17 to 21; 11 open steps have no note. Dependencies live only in prose, so stale waits pile up (goal 3 waits in c44, c46, c27, fixed Oct 26). The whole-roadmap review in the project instructions fires 'at each phase change', and the phase has not changed, so it never ran. Advisor pick, not ruled: (1) build.py prints an upkeep report on each build: notes over 250 words, open steps untouched 5 days, empty notes, steps in the top 5 filed in the last day; no new process, it runs inside the build already called. (2) The trigger for the whole review moves from phase change to each batch merge. (3) A new step names the step it goes ahead of and why, in one line. (4) One rewrite pass on the long notes. No standing triage thread. Full audit: reports/roadmap-upkeep-audit.md in the project files.
